items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1963-03-29
items.q: Thomas Jefferson, Joe Phillip, all those good trumpet players.

ctx.x: Well, I think we're about to run out a little bit now.

Well, let's not leave George McCollum out, Alvin Alcorn. See, as you talk, you think, you see? Think like George McCollum. George McCollum was a, he ain't number one trumpet man, but he was better when you put the music up there too. He was great. I remember one time in Basin, Mississippi, we was playing with Desdun, we was playing the advertisement. George McCollum picked up a number, nobody knew what number and what it was, but it sounds some good. And everybody fell right on in there with him, and the people…

items.title: Ernie Cagnolatti Interview, 1961-04-05
items.q: Joe Phillip started that with me.

ctx.x: Then they have a club out on the airline highway, they call it Cotton Club now. They used to be named. The Rio Rita. The Rio Rita. The Rio Rita. And they wanted to rename the club, so they asked somebody to name the club. And how they rename it up until they did. They still call it Cotton Club. Yeah, still call it Cotton Club. Big club on the airline highway. We used to work there. Yeah. And matter of fact, Mike DeLay was his trumpet player. No, we know how to call him Mike DeLay. Joe Phillip.
Joe Phillip started that with me. Joe Phillip, front of Santiago. Then he left then Mike DeLay.
Yeah. Mike used to play trumpet and Lawrence DeRooks, our Larry band would play piano. When Larry had a job to play, he would put Mike on piano and hire me to play trumpet. Yeah, he played trumpet.
